topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Span to Basis

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows with magnitude and direction.
Scalar multiplication stretches or shrinks a vector.
Vector addition combines vectors via the parallelogram rule.
animations: Draw a vector as an arrow from the origin. (Color: #FF5733)
Label the vector as 'v' near its tip. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight the arrow tip with a glowing effect. (Color: #FFD700)

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
lecture_lines: Linear combinations sum multiple scaled vectors.
Span is the set of all reachable points.
Two non-collinear vectors span the whole plane.
animations: Show two vectors, v and w, originating from origin. (Color: #33FF57)
Animate a scalar multiplication of v by 2. (Color: #3357FF)
Show the vector sum v + w as a diagonal. (Color: #FFFFFF)

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Rule
lecture_lines: Dependence means one vector is redundant.
Redundant vectors lie on the existing span.
Dependent vectors add no new reachable space.
animations: Display three vectors where one is a sum. (Color: #FF33FF)
Flash the redundant vector to highlight dependency. (Color: #FF0000)
Fade out the redundant vector to show subspace. (Color: #808080)

sections.title: Defining the Basis
lecture_lines: A basis is a minimal spanning set.
Basis vectors are always linearly independent.
Basis provides an efficient coordinate system.
animations: Display the standard basis vectors i and j. (Color: #00FFFF)
Highlight the unit square defined by i and j. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Scale the space to show basis flexibility. (Color: #FFFF00)

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
animations: Quickly animate vectors transforming into basis. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Pulse the final graphic to conclude. (Color: #FFFFFF)
